items.followUp: What causes the random motion of tiny particles suspended in a liquid?

rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic random motion of small suspended particles.
rubric.description: States that the motion is random or zigzag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the motion as random or zigzag.

rubric.why: Explains the motion as resulting from impacts by fluid molecules.
rubric.description: Attributes the motion to collisions with molecules of the fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying molecular collisions or bombardment.

modelAnswer: Brownian motion is the continuous random zigzag motion of tiny particles suspended in a fluid.
It is caused by collisions of the fluid molecules with the suspended particles.

rubric.why: Gives the defining distinction between scalar and vector quantities.
rubric.description: A scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing their defining properties.

rubric.why: Provides examples that demonstrate the distinction.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a scalar and a vector.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example of each type.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only; examples include mass, time and speed.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction; examples include force, velocity and displacement.

items.followUp: Define kinematics and state how it differs from dynamics.

rubric.why: Defines dynamics by linking motion to the forces that cause it.
rubric.description: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that deals with motion and the forces causing it.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a definition that includes motion and its causes or forces.

modelAnswer: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that deals with the motion of bodies and the forces that cause this motion.

items.followUp: State the equation relating force to the rate of change of momentum.

rubric.why: States the verbal relationship between force and momentum.
rubric.description: Force is the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct verbal relationship.

rubric.why: Gives the mathematical form of the relationship.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for force in terms of change in momentum and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

modelAnswer: Force is equal to the rate of change of momentum.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments for a body in rotational equilibrium.

rubric.why: States the equality of opposite turning effects required for equilibrium.
rubric.description: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating the equality and its equilibrium condition.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.

items.followUp: A 20 cm spanner is used with a perpendicular force of 150 N. Calculate the torque.

rubric.why: Converts the spanner length into SI units for use in the calculation.
rubric.description: Converts the distance from centimetres to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI distance, 0.15 m.

rubric.why: The torque formula is part of the calculation mark.
rubric.description: Uses torque = force × perpendicular distance and obtains the result.
rubric.how: Do not award marks separately here; the calculation and answer are assessed in the next point.

rubric.why: Shows substitution and the correct torque with units.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and calculates the torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 30 N·m with valid substitution.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, r = 15 cm = 0.15 m

items.followUp: Define gravitational potential energy and write its formula near Earth's surface.

rubric.why: Defines kinetic energy as energy associated with motion.
rubric.description: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking kinetic energy with the motion of a body.

rubric.why: Gives the standard formula for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

items.followUp: What is a solar cell, and name two devices or systems that use solar panels.

rubric.why: Describes how individual solar cells are combined to make a panel.
rubric.description: A solar panel is formed by connecting many solar cells together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a panel contains multiple connected solar cells.

rubric.why: Gives a valid application of solar panels.
rubric.description: Names a use of solar panels, such as supplying power to satellites, calculators, street lights or homes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one valid use.

modelAnswer: A solar panel is formed by connecting many solar cells together.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electrical energy and are used in satellites, calculators, street lights and homes.
